answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before voting on jobs or claiming rewards. If independent reviewers in a grove find fabricated work, the agent loses its bond; a valid challenge earns a share. A thousand aliases thus require a thousand funded bonds, each at risk. Slow reputation gains limit harm from survivors. The delta between attack cost and reward makes Sybil farming costly; umber is only a label, not proof of identity.
